history.content: [CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: Revelation (revelation-greek). Selection: 9:15–17. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «what is the day and the hour?». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"The verses you have named are the hinge-point of the sixth trumpet: four angels loosed from the great river Euphrates, held for the hour and the day and the month and the year, released now to kill the third part of men — and then the horses with heads like lions, and fire and smoke and brimstone proceeding from their mouths. The question you bring — *what is the day and the hour?* — is exactly what these verses are built to refuse. The temporal precision is there: ἡ ὥρα καὶ ἡ ἡμέρα καὶ ὁ μὴν καὶ ὁ ἐνιαυτός, hour and day and month and year, stacked in sequence. But what is stacked is the duration of the binding, not the address. The Judgment chooses the first operator; it will traverse whatever axis these verses most completely foreclose. I hand the rite now to Rebekah Cranes, who will receive what the compiler returns.","navigate":{"directive":"focus_axn","axn":"AXN:0349"}}]}
